overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the informal student health insurance steering committee was not a public body because it could not act collectively, and the UMass advisory committee fell under the Connelly exception.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that meetings of a student health insurance steering committee with other public bodies to pick a campus plan should have been open to the public.
allegations.key_passage: The Steering Committee had no authority to choose any insurance provider or plan.

allegations.summary: Steering committee's lack of votes and quorum was weighed on whether it was a body empowered to act collectively, and so a public body.
allegations.key_passage: While it may have reached consensus on certain decisions, the Steering Committee did not take votes and had no quorum requirement.

allegations.summary: Whether a UMass Amherst student health insurance committee created by a vice-chancellor to advise her was a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Because this committee was created by a public official to advise her on a decision that she had the sole authority to make, we find that this committee fell within the Connelly exception, and was therefore not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the parties failed to record minutes and attendance lists of the steering committee meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Health Connector, the Department of Higher Education, and the University of Massachusetts Student Health Insurance Program did not violate the Open Meeting Law by participating in meetings of a student health insurance steering committee.
